dedupe_keys.name: global road and railway exposure to changing extreme precipitation return periods in a warmer world

description: This study by Kai Liu, Qianzhi Wang, Ming Wang and Elco Koks (Nature Communications, 2023) analyses the global exposure of road and railway assets to changes in extreme precipitation return periods, because transport assets are designed on historical rainfall but serve for decades. Coverage: global road and rail networks from OpenStreetMap, NEX-GDDP downscaled climate projections, and results by World Bank income group. Under about 2 degrees of warming in mid-century (RCP8.5), 43.6% of assets would see at least a 25% fall in design return period (a 33% rise in exceedance probability), rising to 69.9% at about 4 degrees late in the century; nearly 88.4% of assets face more frequent extreme rainfall by mid-century. The authors propose a climate adaptation safety factor in design and find 1.2 sufficient for most regions on the RCP4.5 path. Format and access: open-access article; source data deposited as a DOI dataset and code in the InfExposure repository. Licence and cost: article CC BY 4.0. Caveats: exposure, not damage or disruption, is assessed. It supports hazard exposure screening and climate adaptation of design standards. It relates to GMTRA and the global rail and road climate extremes study in the catalogue.
